_purpose: Registry of calendar hypotheses the Stage-1 figures can render. One entry per hypothesis, so the renderer is hypothesis-general rather than Menghin-only.
_unit_note: unit_total is the headline count in that hypothesis's OWN unit. Never sum across units: Menghin's days (rings x symbols), Schmidt-Kaler's plain ornaments, and Fuls's circle counter are three different things (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 3, Q3).
_status: Only menghin_lunisolar has a full state model today (data/scenarios.json). The others are declared with their unit and target so the comparison figure is honest about what is and is not yet in the data.

hypotheses.title: Menghin (2010) - lunisolar calendar
hypotheses.caveat: The strong 19-year claim is ~20-30%; the intercalary set moves between publications ({5,7,16,17} in 2000, {7,16,17} in 2010). See research/theories/menghin_lunisolar.md.

hypotheses.title: Schmidt-Kaler (2012) - Venus synodic cycle
hypotheses.caveat: Reuses Menghin's zone counts; the reading itself defines no zone colouring, and the ornament tally is NOT a day count. Not to be summed with Menghin's 1783.

hypotheses.title: Lorenz - the structure is the Metonic cycle
hypotheses.caveat: The 19 holds only as disc-bearing bands (measured: 21 zones); the 235 is arithmetic (12x12 + 7x13 for any 12+7 split), so it is not independent evidence.

hypotheses.title: Fuls (2004/2008) - pattern-type correction cycles
hypotheses.unit: rings x symbols, grouped by shared stamp
hypotheses.confidence: candidate, refuted as selective on Berlin
hypotheses.caveat: The arithmetic is real and reproducible, but Fuls's own combinatorial null shows Berlin's hit-rate is indistinguishable from chance; only Schifferstadt is selective. 945 d = 15x59 + 60.

hypotheses.title: Sceptical - ornament, not a demonstrated calendar
hypotheses.caveat: The numbers are easy to hit: free choice of blocks and of intercalary zones makes round targets appear at ~chance rate; the unit is not selective (counting plain symbols hits more often than counting rings).
